post.caption: Hallmark Cards borrowed a goldsmith's stamp. In 1910, Joyce Hall reached Kansas City with two shoeboxes of postcards. His brother Rollie joined him, and the firm was Hall Brothers. In 1915, a fire destroyed their office and all their stock. After the fire, they began making their own card designs. Hall said he liked hallmark, a goldsmith's stamp of quality. It also held his own family name, Hall. By 1928, the name Hallmark was on the back of every card. That year, they became the first greeting card firm to advertise nationally. Hall Brothers became Hallmark Cards in 1954.
